definition: `Essence F ex φ x w`: every property x has at w is necessarily included in φ there, that is, at every world accessible from w every existing individual that has φ has it (AFP definition Essence, φ Ess. x ≡ ❙∀ψ. ψ x ❙⊃ (φ ❙⊃⇩N ψ), with PropertyInclusion φ ❙⊃⇩N ψ ≡ ❙□(❙∀⇧Ey. φ y ❙⊃ ψ y)). Unlike Scott's essence (DEF-ESSENCE-SCOTT) it does not require x to have φ, so the empty property is an essence of everything (STMT-GOEDEL-1970-EMPTY-PROPERTY-IS-ESSENCE), and its inclusion quantifies over existing individuals only. Not the Thomist essence.
